title: Finite quasi-coherent algebras have finitely presented finite approximations with surjective transitions
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $Y$ an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Assume $Y$ is quasi-compact (every open cover of its point space [def-a1-space-point-topology] has a finite subcover) and quasi-separated (its absolute diagonal over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is quasi-compact on affine scheme tests). A morphism is quasi-compact on affine scheme tests when each such pullback has quasi-compact source. Let $\mathcal A$ be a sheaf of commutative $\mathcal O_Y$-algebras on the small etale site whose underlying module is quasi-coherent [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Suppose $\mathcal A$ is finite: for every affine etale chart $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\to Y$, $\mathcal A(U)$ is a finite $R$-module. There exist a small nonempty directed set $I$, quasi-coherent commutative $\mathcal O_Y$-algebras $\mathcal A_i$, algebra maps $\alpha_{ji}:\mathcal A_i\to\mathcal A_j$ for $i\le j$ satisfying the identity and composition laws, and compatible algebra maps $\alpha_i:\mathcal A_i\to\mathcal A$, with the following properties. For every $i$ and every affine etale chart $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\to Y$, $\mathcal A_i(U)$ is finite as an $R$-module and has a presentation $R[T_1,\ldots,T_n]/(f_1,\ldots,f_m)$ with $n,m$ finite. Every transition $\alpha_{ji}$ is surjective on sections on each affine etale chart. The cocone $(\mathcal A,(\alpha_i))$ is colimiting in quasi-coherent commutative $\mathcal O_Y$-algebras [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]: for every such algebra $\mathcal B$, compatible algebra maps $\mathcal A_i\to\mathcal B$ factor uniquely through an algebra map $\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$. Finite presentation here is as an algebra, not as a module.

proof.text: Choose a disjoint affine etale atlas and a finite component subatlas $U_1,\ldots,U_r\to Y$ using the two atlas lemmas. Apply finite-presentation module approximation to the underlying module of $\mathcal A$, obtaining a small filtered diagram $\mathcal F_j\to\mathcal A$. On each $U_a$ its section colimit is $\mathcal A(U_a)$ by affine-chart calculus. Choose finitely many module generators of $\mathcal A(U_a)$ and representatives of these elements at stages of this filtered colimit. There are only finitely many representatives over all $a$, so filteredness gives one stage $j_0$ receiving their stages. Consequently $\mathcal F=\mathcal F_{j_0}\to\mathcal A$ is surjective on each $U_a$, hence as a sheaf map, since these charts cover. Its cokernel is quasi-coherent and zero, so affine-chart calculus makes this map surjective on every affine etale chart. Both topological quasi-compactness and quasi-compactness of the absolute diagonal required by module approximation are precisely the hypotheses on $Y$.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal D=\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal F)$. The linear map just constructed extends uniquely to an algebra map $\psi:\mathcal D\to\mathcal A$. It is surjective on every affine etale chart because its restriction to the degree-one generators already surjects onto the underlying module of $\mathcal A$. Affine-chart calculus gives a quasi-coherent kernel ideal $\mathcal J$ and identifies $\mathcal D/\mathcal J$ with $\mathcal A$, including the quotient algebra universal property.

Let $K$ be the poset of all finite-type quasi-coherent submodules $\mathcal E\subseteq\mathcal J$. It is small in the larger universe: submodules on the fixed small site are families of subsets of the section sets, satisfying module and restriction conditions. It contains $0$; the sum of two members, computed as the image of their direct sum, is a quasi-coherent upper bound, generated on every affine chart by the union of two finite generating lists. To see that these submodules exhaust $\mathcal J$, apply module approximation to $\mathcal J$. The image of each finitely presented stage is quasi-coherent and finite type on every affine chart, hence belongs to $K$. On an affine chart every section of $\mathcal J$ is the image of a stage section, since affine sections compute that filtered colimit. Thus $\mathcal J(V)=\bigcup_{i\in K}\mathcal E_i(V)$ for every affine etale chart $V$; in particular $K$ is a small nonempty directed set.

For $i\in K$ let $\mathcal I_i=(\mathcal E_i)\subseteq\mathcal D$ and $\mathcal Q_i=\mathcal D/\mathcal I_i$. These are quasi-coherent algebra quotients by affine-chart calculus. On $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$, the module $\mathcal F(V)$ is finitely presented and $\mathcal E_i(V)$ is finitely generated. The symmetric-algebra finite-presentation lemma therefore gives a finite algebra presentation of $\mathcal Q_i(V)$: the ideal generated by the latter finite module generating list is finitely generated as an ideal. If $i\le j$ then $\mathcal I_i\subseteq\mathcal I_j$, giving a quotient map $\mathcal Q_i\to\mathcal Q_j$ surjective on affine-chart sections. Quotient maps give identities, composition, and compatible maps to $\mathcal A=\mathcal D/\mathcal J$.

These quotients have colimit $\mathcal A$. Indeed, on an affine chart $V$ every element of $\mathcal J(V)$ lies in some $\mathcal E_i(V)$, and $\mathcal E_i(V)\subseteq\mathcal I_i(V)\subseteq\mathcal J(V)$, so the union of the ideals $\mathcal I_i(V)$ equals $\mathcal J(V)$. A compatible family of maps $\mathcal D(V)/\mathcal I_i(V)\to B$ determines one map from $\mathcal D(V)$: all composites agree, by passing to a common upper bound. It kills this union and therefore factors uniquely through $\mathcal D(V)/\mathcal J(V)=\mathcal A(V)$. This proves the algebra colimit on each affine chart; the cocone criterion in affine-chart calculus proves the colimit in quasi-coherent algebra sheaves.

On each of the finitely many fixed charts $U_a=\operatorname{Spec}R_a$, choose generators $f_{a1},\ldots,f_{an_a}$ of $\mathcal F(U_a)$. Their degree-one images $x_{ab}$ generate $\mathcal D(U_a)$ as an algebra by the symmetric-algebra lemma. Since $\mathcal A(U_a)$ is a finite $R_a$-module, the finite-is-integral lemma gives monic polynomials $P_{ab}\in R_a[T]$ vanishing on the images of $x_{ab}$ in $\mathcal A(U_a)$. Thus $P_{ab}(x_{ab})\in\mathcal J(U_a)$. Step 3 puts each of these finitely many sections in some $\mathcal E_i(U_a)$. Choose a common upper bound $i_0$ for those indices in $K$ (choose $0$ if there are none). For all $i\ge i_0$, every $P_{ab}(x_{ab})$ vanishes in $\mathcal Q_i(U_a)$.

For $i\ge i_0$, the images of the $x_{ab}$ still generate $\mathcal Q_i(U_a)$ as an $R_a$-algebra. Put $d_{ab}=\deg P_{ab}$. If any $d_{ab}=0$, its monic relation is $1=0$, so this section algebra is zero and finite. Otherwise each monic relation replaces $x_{ab}^{d_{ab}}$ by a linear combination of smaller powers; repeated reductions show that the finitely many monomials $\prod_b x_{ab}^{e_b}$ with $0\le e_b<d_{ab}$ span as an $R_a$-module. For no generators the sole monomial is $1$. Thus $\mathcal Q_i$ is finite type as a module on the covering charts, hence etale locally finite type on $Y$; affine-chart calculus gives module finiteness on every affine etale chart. When $Y$ is empty the local assertion is vacuous and its only section modules are zero.

Restrict $K$ to its nonempty directed tail $I=\{i\in K:i\ge i_0\}$ and put $\mathcal A_i=\mathcal Q_i$. All these algebras are now finite and finitely presented, with surjective transitions. The tail retains the colimit: from a compatible tail family, define its map at any $k\in K$ by choosing $l\ge k,i_0$ and composing through $\mathcal Q_l$. A common upper bound of any two such $l$ proves independence; it also proves compatibility. This extends the tail family uniquely to $K$, so the universal property in step 5 gives exactly the required factorization through $\mathcal A$.
